documents_expected.why: RFP: tracks, amounts, cycle, evaluation criteria
MOU, payment tranches and the quarterly and final reports
eligibility details, three-page narrative and budget limit, deadline time

eligibility.rule: Applicant organisations must be based in the U.S.
eligibility.quote: Applicant organizations must reside within the U.S.

eligibility.rule: $25K track: an accredited land trust, or partnered with one
eligibility.quote: Organization should either be an accredited land trust or be working with an accredited land trust as a partner.
alt_quotes: To qualify for the $25K grants, your organization must be an accredited land trust or partnering with an accredited land trust.

eligibility.rule: $10K track: any land trust, or a conservation organisation partnering with one
eligibility.quote: Any land trust (does not need to be accredited) or conservation organization partnering with a land trust may apply.
Project must accomplish or contribute to bird conservation on private lands
these tracks do not fund land or easement acquisition
Project budget must include allowable expenses, such as indirect costs no greater than 10%, a budget justification, and project funds clearly delineated if included within a larger budget.
projects may start between May 1 and September 1 and should be completed within one year.

eligibility.rule: Past awardees must have completed their previous award satisfactorily
eligibility.quote: They must demonstrate a high level of competence, accountability and due diligence, including satisfactory completion of previous award.

documents.item: Online application with a narrative and budget of at most three pages
documents.quote: The narrative text and budget should not go over the allotted three pages, but these supporting materials can be on pages four and beyond.
Project budget must include allowable expenses, such as indirect costs no greater than 10%, a budget justification, and project funds clearly delineated if included within a larger budget.

effort.step: Submit the proposal online when the RFP opens in January (due 1 March, 11:59 p.m.)
effort.quote: This is an annual grant cycle with the RFP for the small grant program opening in January and proposals due by 11:59 p.m. on March 1.
alt_quotes: The RFP closes at 11:59 p.m. on March 1.

effort.step: Sign an MOU with the Cornell Lab to start funding
effort.quote: MOU with list of grant activities, deliverables, and expectations will be signed by the awardee organization and the Cornell Lab of Ornithology to initiate the funding cycle and payment.

co_finance_required.quote: Co-funding is not required, but strong applications will be supplemented by in-kind or partner contributions, matching dollars, or other resources that will leverage the impact of the proposed work.

after_award.quote: Grant recipients are required to submit brief, quarterly progress reports as well as a final report describing the project objectives, methods, results and outcomes, conservation impacts, measures of success, and fiscal expenditures at the end of the year grant period.

notes: The next RFP opens in January 2027; the pages give 1 March as the annual due date without a year, so no due date is recorded. Two tracks: six $10,000 capacity and partnership grants and eight $25,000 management and restoration grants. The gather spent its document budget on privacy and university policy pages instead of the FAQ and expectations pages. The FAQ answers sit in collapsed accordions (in the HTML, not loaded later).
